chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

It is written in the Torah which has not been altered, that Musa (peace be upon him) asked his Lord, saying: 'O Lord! Are You close to me so I may whisper to You, or are You distant so I may call out to You?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Musa! I am the Companion of the one who Mentions Me.'

So Musa said: 'Then who will be in Your Veil on the Day when there is no veil except Your Veil?' He said: 'Those who Mention Me, so I Mention them; and those who love one another for My sake, so I love them. Therefore, they are those whom, whenever I intend to strike the people of the earth with evil, I Remember them, and I repel it from them because of them.'

key_terms.يَتَحَابُّونَ فِيَّ: Loving one another for My sake

ai.seo_question: Who are the people shielded by God's veil on the Day of Judgment according to the Torah?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in al-Kafi's chapter on dhikr, highlights the Shia emphasis on the unaltered Torah (al-Tawrat al-Mubaddala) as a source of theological truth, linking the concept of divine proximity to the communal practice of remembering Allah. It establishes that mutual love for God's sake (al-tahabbud fi Allah) serves as a spiritual shield (sitr) against divine punishment, reinforcing the practical implication that collective dhikr preserves the faithful from calamity.
